  Key Metrics: Cart abandonment rate, Average order value, Checkout completion time
  Stakeholders: Product Management, Marketing, UX Design, Engineering
  Last Updated: 2024-01-26 by Cross-functional Team
  """
  
  Background:
    Given I am logged in as a registered customer
    And I have items in my shopping cart
    And I have selected shipping address
    
  # ============================================================================
  # CHECKOUT FLOW - HAPPY PATH VARIATIONS
  # ============================================================================
  
  @smoke @happy_path
  Scenario: Complete checkout with credit card
    Given I proceed to checkout
    When I select "Credit Card" as payment method
    And I enter valid credit card details:
      | Field         | Value              |
      | Card Number   | 4111 1111 1111 1111 |
      | Expiry        | 12/25              |
      | CVV           | 123                |
      | Name on Card  | John Smith         |
    And I click "Place Order"
    Then my order should be confirmed with number matching pattern "ORD-\\d{8}"
    And I should receive order confirmation email within 2 minutes
    And the order status should be "Processing"
    And inventory should be reserved for ordered items
    
  @payment @integration
  Scenario: Complete checkout with PayPal
    Given I proceed to checkout
    When I select "PayPal" as payment method
    And I authenticate with PayPal credentials
    And I confirm payment in PayPal interface
    Then my order should be confirmed
    And payment should be marked as "Completed" in PayPal
    And I should see PayPal transaction ID
    
  # ============================================================================
  # PAYMENT VALIDATION AND ERROR HANDLING
  # ============================================================================
  
  @validation @security
  Scenario Outline: Credit card validation errors
    Given I proceed to checkout
    When I select "Credit Card" as payment method
    And I enter credit card details:
      | Field         | Value              |
      | Card Number   | <card_number>      |
      | Expiry        | <expiry>           |
      | CVV           | <cvv>              |
    And I click "Place Order"
    Then I should see validation error "<expected_error>"
    And the order should not be placed
    
    Examples: Invalid card numbers
      | card_number       | expiry | cvv | expected_error                     |
      | 1234 5678 9012 3456 | 12/25 | 123 | "Invalid card number"             |
      | 4111 1111 1111 111 | 12/25 | 123 | "Card number must be 16 digits"    |
      |                   | 12/25 | 123 | "Card number is required"          |
    
    Examples: Expiry validation
      | card_number       | expiry | cvv | expected_error                     |
      | 4111 1111 1111 1111 | 01/23 | 123 | "Card has expired"                |
      | 4111 1111 1111 1111 | 13/25 | 123 | "Invalid expiry month"            |
      | 4111 1111 1111 1111 |       | 123 | "Expiry date is required"         |
    
    Examples: CVV validation
      | card_number       | expiry | cvv | expected_error                     |
      | 4111 1111 1111 1111 | 12/25 | 12  | "CVV must be 3 digits"            |
      | 4111 1111 1111 1111 | 12/25 | 12a | "CVV must contain only digits"    |
      | 4111 1111 1111 1111 | 12/25 |     | "CVV is required"                 |
  
  # ============================================================================
  # BUSINESS RULE: PROMOTION AND DISCOUNT APPLICATION
  # ============================================================================
  
  Rule: Promotion codes apply according to business rules
    
    Background:
      Given I have cart total of $200.00
      
    @promotion @business_rules
    Scenario: Apply percentage discount promotion
      Given I have promotion code "SAVE20" with type "percentage" and value "20"
      When I apply promotion code "SAVE20"
      Then cart discount should be "$40.00"
      And cart total should be "$160.00"
      And discount should be visible in order summary
      
    @promotion @edge_case
    Scenario: Promotion code with minimum cart value requirement
      Given I have promotion code "FREESHIP50" requiring minimum cart of $50.00
      And I have cart total of $40.00
      When I apply promotion code "FREESHIP50"
      Then I should see error "Minimum cart value of $50.00 required"
      And promotion should not be applied
      
    @promotion @validation
    Scenario: Expired promotion code
      Given promotion code "WELCOME2023" expired on "2023-12-31"
      When I apply promotion code "WELCOME2023"
      Then I should see error "Promotion code has expired"
      And promotion should not be applied
  
  # ============================================================================
  # INVENTORY VALIDATION DURING CHECKOUT
  # ============================================================================
  
  @inventory @concurrency
  Scenario: Inventory changes during checkout
    Given product "iPhone 15 Pro" has 1 item in stock
    And I have "iPhone 15 Pro" in my cart
    And another customer purchases "iPhone 15 Pro" while I'm checking out
    When I proceed to place my order
    Then I should see error "Sorry, iPhone 15 Pro is no longer available"
    And my cart should be updated to show out-of-stock item

  # ============================================================================
  # TAX AND REGIONAL COMPLIANCE

    When I view order summary

    And tax amount should be "<tax_amount>"
    And total including tax should be "<total_with_tax>"

      | "London, UK EC2A 1AE" | 20% VAT  | £20.00     | £120.00        |
      | "Tokyo, Japan 100-0001" | 10% VAT | ¥1000      | ¥11000         |
  
  # ============================================================================
  # ACCESSIBILITY AND MULTI-LINGUAL SUPPORT
  # ============================================================================
  
  @accessibility @compliance
  Scenario: Checkout accessibility for screen readers
    Given I am using a screen reader
    When I navigate through checkout process
    Then all form fields should have proper ARIA labels
    And error messages should be announced immediately
    And focus should move logically between elements
    And color contrast should meet WCAG 2.1 AA standards
    
  @i18n @localization
  Scenario: Checkout in different languages
    Given my browser language is set to "<language>"
    When I view checkout page
    Then all text should be displayed in "<language>"
    And currency should be displayed as "<currency>"
    And date format should follow "<date_format>" pattern
    
    Examples:
      | language | currency | date_format |
      | French   | €        | DD/MM/YYYY  |
      | German   | €        | DD.MM.YYYY  |
      | Japanese | ¥        | YYYY/MM/DD  |
      | Spanish  | $        | DD/MM/YYYY  |
  
  # ============================================================================
  # PERFORMANCE AND LOAD TESTING SCENARIOS
  # ============================================================================
  
  @performance @non_functional

content.title: Building Scalable Test Automation Architecture
content.explanation: An enterprise-grade Cucumber framework requires careful architectural decisions that balance flexibility, maintainability, and performance. Key architectural components include: Layered Architecture (feature files → step definitions → page objects → services → domain models), Dependency Injection for clean test context management, Configuration Management for multiple environments, Parallel Execution infrastructure, Comprehensive Reporting with business insights, and Integration with existing DevOps toolchain. The framework should support 1000+ scenarios, run in under 15 minutes in CI, provide actionable failure analysis, and generate living documentation that stakeholders actually use.

content.caption: Enterprise Cucumber Framework in Java with Spring Boot
Complete CI/CD Pipeline with BDD Integration
content.code:
# .github/workflows/bdd-pipeline.yml
name: BDD Test Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop, feature/*]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1-5' # Weekdays at 6 AM
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Environment to test'
        required: true
        default: 'staging'
        type: choice
        options:
          - dev
          - staging
          - production
      tags:
        description: 'Cucumber tags to run'
        required: false
        default: '@regression'

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

env:
  JAVA_VERSION: '17'
  NODE_VERSION: '18'
  MAVEN_OPTS: '-Dmaven.repo.local=/tmp/.m2/repository'
  CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_ENABLED: 'true'
  CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN }}

jobs:
  bdd-validation:
    name: Validate Feature Files
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
    
    - name: Setup Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        distribution: 'temurin'
        cache: maven
    
    - name: Validate Gherkin syntax
      run: |
        # Install gherkin-lint
        npm install -g gherkin-lint
        
        # Run validation
        gherkin-lint features/**/*.feature --config .gherkin-lintrc.json
        
        # Check for common issues
        node scripts/validate-features.js
    
    - name: Check for undefined steps
      run: |
        mvn clean compile test-compile \
          -Dcucumber.plugin="pretty" \
          -Dcucumber.features="features" \
          -Dcucumber.glue="steps" \
          -Dcucumber.filter.tags="@validation_only"
    
    - name: Upload validation report
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: feature-validation-report
        path: target/validation-report/

  bdd-smoke-tests:
    name: Smoke Tests
    needs: bdd-validation
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        browser: [chrome, firefox]
      fail-fast: false
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Setup Java and Maven
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        distribution: 'temurin'
        cache: maven
    
    - name: Setup browser
      uses: browser-actions/setup-chrome@v1
      if: matrix.browser == 'chrome'
      with:
        chrome-version: 'latest'
    
    - name: Setup Firefox
      uses: browser-actions/setup-firefox@v1
      if: matrix.browser == 'firefox'
      with:
        firefox-version: 'latest'
    
    - name: Run smoke tests
      run: |
        mvn verify \
          -Denv=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }} \
          -Dbrowser=${{ matrix.browser }} \
          -Dheadless=true \
          -Dcucumber.filter.tags="@smoke" \
          -Dcucumber.plugin="html:target/cucumber-reports/smoke-${{ matrix.browser }}/cucumber.html,json:target/cucumber-reports/smoke-${{ matrix.browser }}/cucumber.json" \
          -Dcucumber.publish.quiet=true
      
    - name: Upload test results
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: smoke-test-results-${{ matrix.browser }}
        path: |
          target/cucumber-reports/smoke-${{ matrix.browser }}/
          target/screenshots/
        retention-days: 7
    
    - name: Publish to Cucumber Reports
      if: always()
      run: |
        # Convert to Cucumber Reports format
        npx cucumber-json-to-html \
          target/cucumber-reports/smoke-${{ matrix.browser }}/cucumber.json \
          target/cucumber-reports/smoke-${{ matrix.browser }}/cucumber.html
    
    - name: Notify on failure
      if: failure()
      uses: rtCamp/action-slack-notify@v2
      env:
        SLACK_WEBHOOK: ${{ secrets.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL }}
        SLACK_CHANNEL: '#bdd-test-failures'
        SLACK_TITLE: 'BDD Smoke Tests Failed'
        SLACK_MESSAGE: 'Smoke tests failed for ${{ matrix.browser }} on ${{ github.ref_name }}'
        SLACK_COLOR: 'danger'

  bdd-regression-tests:
    name: Regression Tests
    needs: [bdd-validation, bdd-smoke-tests]
    if: needs.bdd-smoke-tests.result == 'success'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest-large
    timeout-minutes: 120
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        test-suite: [checkout, payment, inventory, user]
        browser: [chrome]
      max-parallel: 4
      fail-fast: false
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Setup Java
      uses: actions/setup-java@v3
      with:
        java-version: ${{ env.JAVA_VERSION }}
        distribution: 'temurin'
        cache: maven
    
    - name: Setup Chrome
      uses: browser-actions/setup-chrome@v1
      with:
        chrome-version: 'latest'
    
    - name: Run parallel tests
      run: |
        # Generate unique run ID
        RUN_ID="${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-${{ matrix.test-suite }}"
        
        mvn verify \
          -Denv=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }} \
          -Dbrowser=${{ matrix.browser }} \
          -Dheadless=true \
          -Dparallel=true \
          -DthreadCount=4 \
          -Dcucumber.filter.tags="@${{ matrix.test-suite }} and @regression" \
          -Dcucumber.plugin="html:target/cucumber-reports/${{ matrix.test-suite }}/cucumber.html,json:target/cucumber-reports/${{ matrix.test-suite }}/cucumber.json,timeline:target/cucumber-reports/${{ matrix.test-suite }}/timeline" \
          -Dcucumber.execution.parallel.config.fixed.parallelism=4 \
          -Dcucumber.execution.parallel.config.fixed.max-pool-size=8 \
          -Dcucumber.publish.name="Regression - ${{ matrix.test-suite }}" \
          -Dcucumber.publish.batch.id="$RUN_ID" \
          -Dcucumber.publish.batch.name="${{ github.workflow }} - ${{ github.ref_name }}"
      
    - name: Generate living documentation
      if: always()
      run: |
        # Merge all JSON reports
        npx cucumber-json-merge \
          target/cucumber-reports/**/cucumber.json \
          -o target/cucumber-reports/combined/cucumber.json
        
        # Generate HTML report
        npx cucumber-html-reporter \
          --jsonDir target/cucumber-reports/combined \
          --reportDir target/cucumber-reports/living-docs \
          --metadata.browser=${{ matrix.browser }} \
          --metadata.env=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }} \
          --metadata.version=${{ github.sha }}
      
    - name: Upload living documentation
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: living-documentation-${{ matrix.test-suite }}
        path: target/cucumber-reports/living-docs/
        retention-days: 30
    
    - name: Publish to S3
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && success()
      run: |
        aws s3 sync \
          target/cucumber-reports/living-docs/ \
          s3://bdd-living-docs/${{ github.sha }}/ \
          --acl public-read
      env:
        AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
        AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
        AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1

  bdd-metrics-and-reporting:
    name: Metrics and Reporting
    needs: [bdd-smoke-tests, bdd-regression-tests]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    
    steps:
    - name: Download all test results
      uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
      with:
        path: artifacts
        pattern: '*'
        merge-multiple: true
    
    - name: Generate metrics dashboard
      run: |
        node scripts/generate-metrics.js \
          --input artifacts \
          --output metrics-dashboard \
          --commit ${{ github.sha }} \
          --branch ${{ github.ref_name }} \
          --pr ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || 'none' }}
      
    - name: Generate BDD health report
      run: |
        node scripts/bdd-health-report.js \
          --features features/ \
          --step-definitions src/test/java/steps/ \
          --output bdd-health-report.html
      
    - name: Upload metrics
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: bdd-metrics-dashboard
        path: |
          metrics-dashboard/
          bdd-health-report.html
        retention-days: 90
    
    - name: Post metrics to Slack
      if: always()
      run: |
        node scripts/post-metrics-to-slack.js \
          --metrics metrics-dashboard/summary.json \
          --webhook ${{ secrets.SLACK_METRICS_WEBHOOK }}
    
    - name: Update BDD adoption dashboard
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
      run: |
        # Update centralized dashboard
        echo "Updating BDD adoption metrics..."

  bdd-gates:
    name: Quality Gates
    needs: [bdd-metrics-and-reporting]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
    - name: Check quality gates
      run: |
        node scripts/check-quality-gates.js \
          --metrics metrics-dashboard/summary.json \
          --gates .quality-gates.json
      
    - name: Fail if gates not met
      if: failure()
      run: |
        echo "❌ Quality gates not met"
        echo "Check the BDD metrics dashboard for details"
        exit 1

# Docker configuration for test environment
docker-compose.bdd.yml
version: '3.8'

services:
  bdd-test-runner:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.bdd
    environment:
      - TEST_ENV=staging

      - HEADLESS=true

  wiremock:

Remember that step definitions should be thin—they should delegate to helper classes and domain objects rather than containing complex logic.

    - name: Run BDD tests
      run: |
        npm run test:ci \
          --world-parameters="{\"environment\":\"${{ matrix.env }}\",\"browser\":\"${{ matrix.browser }}\"}" \
          --tags="@${{ matrix.env }} and not @wip"
      env:

content.title: What is Visual Regression Testing?
content.explanation: Visual Regression Testing (VRT) is a quality assurance methodology that detects unintended visual changes in user interfaces by comparing screenshots of the application's UI against baseline images. Unlike functional testing that validates behaviors and logic, VRT focuses exclusively on the visual presentation layer. It works by taking baseline screenshots (approved visual states) and comparing them with new screenshots taken during testing. When differences exceed configured thresholds, tests fail, alerting teams to visual regressions before they reach users. VRT is particularly valuable for catching CSS bugs, layout issues, responsive design problems, and visual inconsistencies that functional tests often miss.

items.definition: Reference screenshots representing the approved visual state of the application. These serve as the 'gold standard' for comparison. Baselines are version-controlled and require explicit approval to update. Best practice: Store baselines separately from test code with clear versioning and metadata.

The most basic form of visual comparison that examines each pixel's color value. While simple, pixel comparison is brittle—small changes like anti-aliasing, rendering differences, or timestamps cause failures. Use with caution, typically only for static content or when pixel-perfect accuracy is required.

Comparison method focusing on element positioning and structure rather than exact pixel colors. Tolerates minor rendering differences while detecting significant layout shifts. Ideal for responsive design testing where exact pixel positions may vary across devices and browsers.

Method that ignores styling and colors, focusing only on text content and element presence. Useful for content-heavy applications where styling may change but content should remain consistent, or for accessibility testing where content structure matters more than visual presentation.

Advanced comparison using machine learning to understand visual semantics. Can distinguish intentional design changes from bugs, ignore dynamic content, and identify accessibility issues. Tools like Applitools Eyes use this approach to provide 'smart' comparisons that reduce false positives.

Configurable sensitivity setting determining how strictly screenshots are compared. Common levels: Strict (exact pixels), Content (ignore colors), Layout (structure only), Exact (pixel-perfect). Choosing appropriate match levels based on test context reduces false positives while maintaining detection sensitivity.

Designated areas of screenshots excluded from comparison. Essential for handling dynamic content like timestamps, user-specific data, or rotating banners. Can be defined using static coordinates, CSS selectors, or visual AI pattern recognition. Best practice: Use data attributes to mark dynamic elements.

Areas allowed to move within a tolerance range without causing test failure. Useful for elements with minor positional variations like tooltips, dropdowns, animated components, or content that may shift slightly due to rendering differences. Configure with pixel tolerance thresholds.

steps.title: Assess Your Visual Testing Needs
steps.description: Identify what types of visual issues matter most for your application
steps.details: Analyze past UI bugs and regression patterns. Identify critical user journeys that must remain visually consistent. Determine which viewports and browsers matter most. Consider team skills and tooling budget. Document success criteria for visual testing implementation.

steps.details: For enterprise needs: Applitools (AI-powered, comprehensive features). For open-source preference: Percy (good free tier, GitHub integration). For component libraries: Chromatic (Storybook integration). For custom needs: Resemble.js or pixelmatch libraries. Consider: learning curve, CI/CD integration, reporting capabilities, and pricing model.

steps.title: Set Up Test Environment and Configuration
steps.description: Configure browsers, viewports, and testing framework integration
steps.details: Use consistent browser versions (Chrome 120+, Firefox 115+, etc.). Define viewport sizes covering desktop, tablet, and mobile breakpoints. Integrate with your test runner (Jest, Mocha, Cypress, Playwright). Set up API keys and environment variables securely. Configure match levels and comparison thresholds.

steps.title: Create Baseline Screenshots
steps.description: Capture initial reference images of your application in known-good state
steps.details: Run tests against a stable, production-like environment. Save screenshots as version-controlled baselines. Tag baselines with version numbers and metadata. Store in dedicated repository or cloud service. Establish baseline approval process with design/UX teams.

steps.title: Configure Comparison Settings and Ignore Regions
steps.description: Set match levels, ignore regions, floating regions, and failure thresholds
steps.details: Choose appropriate match level (Layout for most cases). Define ignore regions for dynamic content using CSS selectors. Set floating regions for elements with positional variation. Configure failure thresholds (pixel difference percentage). Implement retry logic for flaky renders.

steps.title: Integrate with Existing Test Suites
steps.description: Add visual assertions to your functional tests strategically
steps.details: Add visual checkpoints after key interactions and page loads. Combine visual and functional assertions for comprehensive coverage. Use page objects to define screenshot regions consistently. Implement visual tests at different testing pyramid levels. Balance test coverage with execution time.

steps.title: Establish Approval and Baseline Management Workflow
steps.description: Create processes for reviewing and approving visual changes
steps.details: Define roles and responsibilities for baseline approval. Implement pull request reviews for visual changes. Create dashboard for visualizing differences. Set up notifications for visual test failures. Establish process for intentional vs unintentional change classification.

steps.title: Implement CI/CD Integration and Monitoring
steps.description: Automate visual testing in your pipeline with proper reporting
steps.details: Add visual tests to PR checks and main branch builds. Configure automated baseline updates for approved changes. Set up approval workflows with design team integration. Implement Slack/Teams notifications for failures. Monitor visual test performance and effectiveness metrics.

content.title: Visual Testing Tools and Implementation Patterns
Choosing the Right Visual Testing Tool
content.explanation: The visual testing landscape offers solutions ranging from simple screenshot comparison libraries to AI-powered enterprise platforms. Your choice depends on several factors: budget constraints, team size and skill level, application complexity, integration needs with existing tooling, and specific requirements like cross-browser testing or component-level validation. Open-source solutions like Percy and BackstopJS offer good basic functionality with generous free tiers but may require more maintenance. Commercial tools like Applitools provide advanced features like visual AI, cross-browser grids, and comprehensive dashboards but come with higher costs. For component-level testing in design systems, Chromatic integrates seamlessly with Storybook. Consider not just the tool's features but also its learning curve, community support, long-term maintenance requirements, and how well it fits into your existing development workflow.

content.title: Advanced Visual Testing Strategies & CI/CD Integration
Enterprise-Grade Visual Testing Architecture
content.explanation: For organizations at scale, visual testing must evolve from simple screenshot comparisons to a comprehensive quality assurance system. This involves several key architectural considerations: 1) Multi-tool strategy - Using different tools for different purposes (Applitools for AI-powered comparisons, Percy for PR reviews, Chromatic for components). 2) Distributed execution - Running tests across multiple browsers, devices, and viewports in parallel using cloud grids. 3) Intelligent baselining - Automated baseline updates for intentional changes with required approvals for significant visual shifts. 4) Integration with design systems - Connecting visual tests to Figma/Sketch designs for design-to-code validation. 5) Predictive analytics - Using historical data to predict which changes are likely to cause visual regressions. 6) Self-healing tests - Automated updates for trivial changes like timestamp updates or minor spacing adjustments. The architecture should support thousands of visual tests running in under 15 minutes in CI, provide actionable failure analysis, and generate living documentation that stakeholders actually use.

content.code:
# .github/workflows/visual-regression.yml
name: Visual Regression Testing Pipeline

description: |
  Comprehensive visual regression testing pipeline that:
  - Validates visual consistency across browsers and devices
  - Integrates with design team approval workflows
  - Generates living documentation
  - Provides actionable failure analysis

on:
  # Trigger on pull requests to main branches
  pull_request:
    branches: [main, develop, release/*]
    paths:
      - 'src/**'
      - 'public/**'
      - 'styles/**'
      - 'package.json'
      - 'package-lock.json'
  
  # Trigger on push to main for scheduled runs
  push:
    branches: [main]
  
  # Scheduled runs for baseline maintenance
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 8 * * 1-5' # Weekday mornings at 8 AM
  
  # Manual trigger with parameters
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: 'Environment to test against'
        required: true
        default: 'staging'
        type: choice
        options: [dev, staging, production]
      browsers:
        description: 'Browsers to test'
        required: false
        default: 'chrome,firefox'
        type: string
      viewports:
        description: 'Viewports to test'
        required: false
        default: 'desktop,tablet,mobile'
        type: string
      tags:
        description: 'Cucumber tags to run'
        required: false
        default: '@visual'
        type: string

# Global environment variables
evars:
  NODE_VERSION: '18.x'
  JAVA_VERSION: '17'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  
  # Tool API keys (secrets)
  APPLITOOLS_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.APPLITOOLS_API_KEY }}
  PERCY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PERCY_TOKEN }}
  CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN }}
  
  # Reporting configuration
  CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_ENABLED: 'true'
  CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CUCUMBER_PUBLISH_TOKEN }}
  
  # Test configuration
  VISUAL_TEST_TIMEOUT: '300000' # 5 minutes
  PARALLEL_THREADS: '4'
  RETRY_ATTEMPTS: '2'
  
  # URLs
  TEST_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.TEST_BASE_URL || 'https://staging.example.com' }}
  API_BASE_URL: ${{ vars.API_BASE_URL || 'https://api.staging.example.com' }}

# Job configurations
jobs:
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  # STAGE 1: PREPARATION AND VALIDATION
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  
  validate-features:
    name: Validate Feature Files and Configuration
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        fetch-depth: 0
        ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
    
    - name: Setup Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}
        cache: 'npm'
    
    - name: Install dependencies
      run: |
        npm ci
        npm install -g gherkin-lint cucumber-html-reporter
    
    - name: Validate Gherkin syntax
      run: |
        # Check for syntax errors
        gherkin-lint features/visual/**/*.feature --config .gherkin-lintrc.json
        
        # Check for undefined steps
        npx cucumber-js --dry-run --format=summary features/visual/
        
        # Validate visual test configuration
        node scripts/validate-visual-config.js
    
    - name: Check for visual testing markers
      run: |
        # Look for files that should trigger visual tests
        CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || 'HEAD~1' }} ${{ github.sha }})
        echo "Changed files:\n$CHANGED_FILES"
        
        # Check if visual tests should run
        if echo "$CHANGED_FILES" | grep -q -E '\.(css|scss|less|jsx|tsx|html|vue)$'; then
          echo "Visual tests required: UI files changed"
          echo "VISUAL_TESTS_REQUIRED=true" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        elif echo "$CHANGED_FILES" | grep -q -E 'features/visual/'; then
          echo "Visual tests required: Feature files changed"
          echo "VISUAL_TESTS_REQUIRED=true" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        else
          echo "Visual tests not required"
          echo "VISUAL_TESTS_REQUIRED=false" >> $GITHUB_ENV
        fi
    
    - name: Upload validation report
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: validation-report
        path: |
          reports/validation/
          .gherkin-lint.log

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  # STAGE 2: VISUAL TESTS EXECUTION
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  
  visual-smoke-tests:
    name: Visual Smoke Tests
    needs: validate-features
    if: needs.validate-features.outputs.VISUAL_TESTS_REQUIRED == 'true' || github.event_name == 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        browser: [chrome]
        viewport: [desktop]
      fail-fast: false
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
    
    - name: Setup test environment
      uses: ./.github/actions/setup-visual-testing
      with:
        browser: ${{ matrix.browser }}
        viewport: ${{ matrix.viewport }}
    
    - name: Run visual smoke tests
      run: |
        npm run test:visual:smoke \
          --browser=${{ matrix.browser }} \
          --viewport=${{ matrix.viewport }} \
          --env=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }} \
          --batch-name="Smoke Tests - ${{ github.workflow }} - ${{ github.sha }}" \
          --batch-id="${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}"
      env:
        APPLITOOLS_BATCH_NOTIFY: true
        APPLITOOLS_DONT_CLOSE_BATCHES: true
    
    - name: Upload test results
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: visual-smoke-results-${{ matrix.browser }}-${{ matrix.viewport }}
        path: |
          test-results/visual/smoke/
          screenshots/
          applitools-report.json
        retention-days: 7

  visual-regression-tests:
    name: Visual Regression Tests
    needs: [validate-features, visual-smoke-tests]
    if: needs.visual-smoke-tests.result == 'success' && (github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'schedule')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest-large
    timeout-minutes: 90
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        test-suite: [homepage, product, checkout, dashboard]
        browser: [chrome, firefox]
        viewport: [desktop, tablet]
      max-parallel: 8
      fail-fast: false
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
      with:
        ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
    
    - name: Setup parallel test environment
      uses: ./.github/actions/setup-visual-testing
      with:
        browser: ${{ matrix.browser }}
        viewport: ${{ matrix.viewport }}
        parallel: true
    
    - name: Run visual regression tests
      run: |
        npm run test:visual:regression \
          --suite=${{ matrix.test-suite }} \
          --browser=${{ matrix.browser }} \
          --viewport=${{ matrix.viewport }} \
          --parallel=${{ env.PARALLEL_THREADS }} \
          --retry=${{ env.RETRY_ATTEMPTS }} \
          --env=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }} \
          --batch-name="Regression - ${{ matrix.test-suite }} - ${{ github.workflow }}" \
          --batch-id="${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}-${{ matrix.test-suite }}"
      env:
        APPLITOOLS_BATCH_NOTIFY: true
        TEST_TIMEOUT: ${{ env.VISUAL_TEST_TIMEOUT }}
    
    - name: Process test results
      if: always()
      run: |
        # Merge JSON reports
        npx cucumber-json-merge \
          test-results/visual/regression/**/*.json \
          -o test-results/visual/combined/${{ matrix.test-suite }}-${{ matrix.browser }}-${{ matrix.viewport }}.json
        
        # Generate HTML report
        npx cucumber-html-reporter \
          --jsonDir test-results/visual/combined \
          --reportDir reports/visual/${{ matrix.test-suite }} \
          --metadata.browser=${{ matrix.browser }} \
          --metadata.viewport=${{ matrix.viewport }} \
          --metadata.suite=${{ matrix.test-suite }} \
          --metadata.env=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }}
    
    - name: Upload regression results
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: visual-regression-${{ matrix.test-suite }}-${{ matrix.browser }}-${{ matrix.viewport }}
        path: |
          test-results/visual/regression/
          reports/visual/${{ matrix.test-suite }}/
          screenshots/
        retention-days: 14

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  # STAGE 3: CROSS-BROWSER AND ACCESSIBILITY VALIDATION
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  
  cross-browser-visual-tests:
    name: Cross-Browser Visual Tests
    needs: visual-regression-tests
    if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == 'main')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 120
    
    strategy:
      matrix:
        browser:
          - { name: 'chrome', version: 'latest' }
          - { name: 'firefox', version: 'latest' }
          - { name: 'safari', version: 'latest' }
          - { name: 'edge', version: 'latest' }
      fail-fast: false
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Setup cross-browser testing
      uses: browser-actions/setup-${{ matrix.browser.name }}@v1
      with:
        ${{ matrix.browser.name }}-version: ${{ matrix.browser.version }}
    
    - name: Run cross-browser visual tests
      run: |
        npm run test:visual:cross-browser \
          --browser=${{ matrix.browser.name }} \
          --browser-version=${{ matrix.browser.version }} \
          --env=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }} \
          --accessibility=true \
          --batch-name="Cross-Browser - ${{ matrix.browser.name }}"
      env:
        APPLITOOLS_ULTRAFAST_GRID: true
        APPLITOOLS_CONCURRENCY: 10
    
    - name: Generate cross-browser report
      if: always()
      run: |
        node scripts/generate-cross-browser-report.js \
          --browser=${{ matrix.browser.name }} \
          --output=reports/cross-browser/${{ matrix.browser.name }}.html
    
    - name: Upload cross-browser results
      if: always()
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: cross-browser-${{ matrix.browser.name }}
        path: |
          test-results/cross-browser/
          reports/cross-browser/
        retention-days: 30

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  # STAGE 4: REPORTING AND APPROVAL WORKFLOW
  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  
  visual-test-reporting:
    name: Visual Test Reporting
    needs: [visual-regression-tests, cross-browser-visual-tests]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    timeout-minutes: 15
    
    steps:
    - name: Download all test results
      uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
      with:
        path: artifacts
        pattern: '*'
        merge-multiple: true
    
    - name: Generate comprehensive report
      run: |
        node scripts/generate-visual-report.js \
          --input artifacts \
          --output reports/comprehensive \
          --commit ${{ github.sha }} \
          --branch ${{ github.ref_name }} \
          --pr ${{ github.event.pull_request.number || 'none' }} \
          --env ${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }}
    
    - name: Generate living documentation
      run: |
        # Create HTML documentation
        npx multiple-cucumber-html-reporter \
          --jsonDir artifacts \
          --reportPath reports/living-docs \
          --metadata.browser="Multiple" \
          --metadata.env=${{ github.event.inputs.environment || 'staging' }} \
          --metadata.version=${{ github.sha }}
        
        # Generate executive summary
        node scripts/generate-executive-summary.js \
          --input reports/comprehensive \
          --output reports/executive-summary.html
    
    - name: Upload comprehensive reports
      uses: actions/upload-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: visual-test-reports
        path: |
          reports/comprehensive/
          reports/living-docs/
          reports/executive-summary.html
        retention-days: 90
    
    - name: Publish to S3 (for living documentation)
      if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && success()
      run: |
        aws s3 sync \
          reports/living-docs/ \
          s3://visual-testing-docs/${{ github.sha }}/ \
          --acl public-read \
          --cache-control "max-age=3600"
      env:
        AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID: ${{ secrets.AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID }}
        AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY: ${{ secrets.AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY }}
        AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1

  visual-approval-workflow:
    name: Visual Approval Workflow
    needs: visual-test-reporting
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && needs.visual-test-reporting.result == 'failure'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    
    steps:
    - name: Checkout code
      uses: actions/checkout@v3
    
    - name: Download test results
      uses: actions/download-artifact@v3
      with:
        name: visual-test-reports
        path: reports
    
    - name: Generate visual diff report
      run: |
        node scripts/generate-diff-report.js \
          --reports reports/comprehensive \
          --output visual-diff-report.html
    
    - name: Create approval request comment
      uses: actions/github-script@v6
      with:
        script: |
          const fs = require('fs');
          const report = fs.readFileSync('visual-diff-report.html', 'utf8');
          
          // Parse visual differences from report
          const differences = []; // This would parse actual differences
          
          let comment = `## 🔍 Visual Regression Test Results\n`;
          comment += `**Status**: ❌ Visual differences detected\n`;
          comment += `**Commit**: ${context.sha}\n`;
          comment += `**Branch**: ${context.ref}\n`;
          comment += `**Test Environment**: ${process.env.TEST_ENV || 'staging'}\n\n`;
          
          if (differences.length > 0) {
            comment += `### 📊 Detected Visual Differences\n`;
            differences.forEach(diff => {
              comment += `- **${diff.page}** (${diff.viewport}): ${diff.diffPercentage}% different\n`;
              comment += `  - [View Diff](${diff.diffUrl})\n`;
              comment += `  - [Baseline](${diff.baselineUrl})\n`;
              comment += `  - [Checkpoint](${diff.checkpointUrl})\n`;
            });
          }
          
          comment += `\n### 👥 Approval Required\n`;
          comment += `Please review the visual differences and:\n`;
          comment += `1. **Approve** if changes are intentional and correct\n`;
          comment += `2. **Update baselines** after approval\n`;
          comment += `3. **Fix** if changes are regressions\n\n`;
          
          comment += `### 📋 Approval Checklist\n`;
          comment += `- [ ] **Design Team**: Changes align with design system\n`;
          comment += `- [ ] **Product Team**: Changes meet business requirements\n`;
          comment += `- [ ] **Accessibility**: Changes maintain accessibility standards\n`;
          comment += `- [ ] **Cross-browser**: Changes work across all supported browsers\n\n`;
          
          // Add reaction buttons for approval
          comment += `<!-- visual-approval-workflow -->\n`;
          comment += `**React with**: 👍 Approve | 👎 Reject | 🤔 Needs Discussion\n`;
          
          github.rest.issues.createComment({
            issue_number: context.issue.number,
            owner: context.repo.owner,
            repo: context.repo.repo,
            body: comment
          });
    
    - name: Notify teams for approval
      uses: 8398a7/action-slack@v3
      with:
        status: custom
        channel: '#visual-testing-approvals'
        fields: workflow,job,commit,message,author
        custom_payload: |
          {

              {

                "title": "Visual Approval Required",
                "title_link": "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/pull/${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}",
                "text": "Visual differences detected in PR #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}. Please review and approve.",
                "fields": [
                  {
                    "title": "PR",
                    "value": "#${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}",
                    "short": true
                  },
                  {
                    "title": "Author",
                    "value": "${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login }}",
                    "short": true
                  }
                ]
              }
            ]
          }
      env:
        SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL: ${{ secrets.SLACK_APPROVAL_WEBHOOK_URL }}

  # -----------------------------------------------------------------
  # STAGE 5: QUALITY GATES AND METRICS

    - name: Upload metrics

      with:

        path: |

        retention-days: 90
    
    - name: Update monitoring dashboard

content.title: Optimizing Visual Test Execution Performance
content.explanation: Visual testing can become performance-intensive as test suites grow. Optimizing execution involves strategies for parallelization, selective testing, intelligent batching, and resource management. Key considerations include reducing unnecessary screenshots, optimizing comparison algorithms, implementing efficient baseline management, and leveraging cloud infrastructure for distributed execution. Performance bottlenecks typically occur in screenshot capture, image comparison, network latency, and storage operations.

content.title: Performance Optimization Strategies Matrix
rows: Run only visual tests for changed components/pages
Group related tests to share setup/teardown
Only capture screenshots after interactions complete
Cache baseline images, DOM snapshots, resources
Reuse browser instances across test suites
Use hardware acceleration, WebGL for image diff
Run critical paths first, non-critical async

content.caption: Intelligent Test Selection and Parallel Execution Engine

steps.title: Analyze Current Performance Bottlenecks
steps.description: Identify where your visual tests are spending the most time
steps.details: Use profiling tools to measure screenshot capture time, image comparison time, network latency, and resource consumption. Identify tests with flaky behavior causing retries. Document baseline performance metrics for comparison after optimizations.

steps.title: Implement Selective Test Execution
steps.description: Run only tests affected by code changes
steps.details: Integrate with version control to detect changed files. Map file changes to affected visual tests. Use dependency analysis to determine test scope. Implement fallback mechanisms for edge cases.

steps.title: Set Up Parallel Execution Infrastructure
steps.description: Distribute tests across multiple workers and browsers
steps.details: Configure Selenium Grid or cloud testing services. Implement worker pool with resource monitoring. Balance test distribution based on resource requirements. Handle test isolation and cleanup between parallel runs.

steps.title: Optimize Screenshot Capture and Comparison
steps.description: Reduce screenshot size and optimize comparison algorithms
steps.details: Capture only necessary viewport areas. Implement intelligent waiting for stability. Use hardware-accelerated image processing. Cache comparison results for identical screenshots.

steps.title: Implement Caching and Incremental Testing
steps.description: Cache test results and baselines to avoid redundant work
steps.details: Cache baseline images locally. Implement incremental baseline updates. Store comparison results with versioning. Invalidate cache based on dependency changes.

steps.title: Monitor and Adjust Optimization Strategies
steps.description: Continuously monitor performance and adjust strategies
steps.details: Set up performance dashboards. Track optimization effectiveness over time. Implement A/B testing for optimization strategies. Establish performance budgets and alerts.

content.title: Handling Dynamic Content and Eliminating Flaky Tests
Strategies for Stable Visual Testing with Dynamic Content
content.explanation: Dynamic content poses significant challenges for visual testing, causing false positives and flaky tests. Effective strategies involve identifying dynamic elements, implementing intelligent masking, using stable selectors, and leveraging AI-powered comparison tools. Key dynamic content types include: timestamps, user-specific data, rotating banners, live feeds, advertisements, A/B test variations, and data that changes based on external factors like stock prices or weather.

Mark dynamic elements with data attributes

content.title: Combining Visual Testing with Accessibility Validation
content.explanation: Visual testing and accessibility testing are complementary disciplines that together ensure both the visual appearance and usability of applications for all users. By integrating accessibility checks into visual testing workflows, teams can catch accessibility violations that have visual manifestations, such as insufficient color contrast, improper text sizing, missing focus indicators, and layout issues that affect screen reader users. Modern visual testing tools can detect accessibility issues through AI analysis of screenshots, DOM inspection, and integration with dedicated accessibility testing libraries.

content.title: Accessibility Issues Detectable Through Visual Testing
rows: Text hard to read against background
No visible focus rings on interactive elements
Inconsistent font sizes, poor visual hierarchy

content.title: Cross-Browser and Cross-Device Testing at Scale
Managing Visual Consistency Across Multiple Platforms
content.explanation: Cross-browser and cross-device visual testing ensures consistent user experiences across the diverse ecosystem of browsers, operating systems, and devices. This involves testing on different browser engines (WebKit, Gecko, Blink), various operating systems (Windows, macOS, iOS, Android, Linux), multiple device types (desktop, tablet, mobile), and different screen densities (1x, 2x, 3x). The challenges include rendering differences, CSS feature support variations, font rendering discrepancies, and hardware acceleration differences. Effective strategies involve prioritized browser matrices, responsive design testing, and intelligent comparison that accounts for acceptable platform-specific variations.

Leveraging AI for Smarter Visual Testing
content.explanation: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning are revolutionizing visual testing by enabling smarter comparison, automatic anomaly detection, and predictive analysis. AI-powered visual testing tools can distinguish between intentional design changes and actual bugs, automatically ignore dynamic content, detect accessibility issues, and predict which code changes are likely to cause visual regressions. Key AI applications in visual testing include: computer vision for content understanding, natural language processing for text analysis, anomaly detection for unexpected changes, and predictive analytics for risk assessment.

# ai_visual_testing.py
# Advanced AI-powered visual testing using computer vision

import cv2
import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow import keras
from sklearn.ensemble import IsolationForest
import pytesseract
from difflib import SequenceMatcher
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Optional
import json

class AIVisualTester:
    """
    AI-powered visual testing system combining computer vision,
    OCR, and machine learning for intelligent visual comparisons.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, config: Dict = None):
        self.config = config or {
            'model_path': './models/visual_testing_model.h5',
            'confidence_threshold': 0.85,
            'use_ocr': True,
            'use_object_detection': True,
            'enable_anomaly_detection': True,
            'text_similarity_threshold': 0.9
        }
        
        # Load ML models
        self.models = self.load_models()
        
        # Initialize anomaly detector
        self.anomaly_detector = IsolationForest(contamination=0.1, random_state=42)
        self.feature_vectors = []
        
    def load_models(self) -> Dict:
        """Load pre-trained ML models for visual testing."""
        models = {}
        
        try:
            # Load object detection model
            models['object_detector'] = self.load_object_detection_model()
            
            # Load semantic segmentation model
            models['segmenter'] = self.load_segmentation_model()
            
            # Load change classification model
            models['change_classifier'] = self.load_change_classifier()
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Warning: Could not load all models: {e}")
            
        return models
    
    def compare_with_ai(self, baseline_img: np.ndarray, 
                       current_img: np.ndarray, 
                       metadata: Dict = None) -> Dict:
        """
        Perform AI-powered comparison between baseline and current images.
        """
        results = {
            'status': 'unknown',
            'differences': [],
            'confidence': 0.0,
            'ai_analysis': {},
            'recommendations': []
        }
        
        # 1. Basic structural comparison
        structural_diff = self.compare_structural(baseline_img, current_img)
        results['structural_difference'] = structural_diff
        
        # 2. Object detection and comparison
        if self.config['use_object_detection'] and 'object_detector' in self.models:
            object_results = self.compare_objects(baseline_img, current_img)
            results['object_comparison'] = object_results
            results['differences'].extend(object_results.get('differences', []))
        
        # 3. Text content comparison using OCR
        if self.config['use_ocr']:
            text_results = self.compare_text_content(baseline_img, current_img)
            results['text_comparison'] = text_results
            
            # Add text differences if significant
            if text_results['similarity'] < self.config['text_similarity_threshold']:
                results['differences'].append({
                    'type': 'text_change',
                    'confidence': 1 - text_results['similarity'],
                    'details': text_results
                })
        
        # 4. Semantic segmentation for understanding regions
        if 'segmenter' in self.models:
            semantic_results = self.compare_semantic(baseline_img, current_img)
            results['semantic_comparison'] = semantic_results
            
            # Detect region changes
            region_changes = self.detect_region_changes(semantic_results)
            if region_changes:
                results['differences'].extend(region_changes)
        
        # 5. Classify changes using ML model
        if 'change_classifier' in self.models:
            change_classification = self.classify_changes(
                baseline_img, current_img, results['differences']
            )
            results['change_classification'] = change_classification
            
            # Update status based on classification
            if change_classification['is_intentional']:
                results['status'] = 'approved_change'
                results['confidence'] = change_classification['confidence']
            elif change_classification['is_bug']:
                results['status'] = 'bug_detected'
                results['confidence'] = change_classification['confidence']
        
        # 6. Anomaly detection
        if self.config['enable_anomaly_detection']:
            anomaly_result = self.detect_anomaly(results)
            if anomaly_result['is_anomaly']:
                results['status'] = 'anomaly_detected'
                results['anomaly_analysis'] = anomaly_result
        
        # 7. Generate recommendations
        results['recommendations'] = self.generate_recommendations(results)
        
        # Determine final status
        if results['status'] == 'unknown':
            if len(results['differences']) == 0:
                results['status'] = 'identical'
            else:
                results['status'] = 'differences_found'
        
        return results
    
    def compare_structural(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:
        """Compare structural similarity using SSIM and feature matching."""
        # Convert to grayscale for structural comparison
        gray1 = cv2.cvtColor(img1, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        gray2 = cv2.cvtColor(img2, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        
        # Calculate Structural Similarity Index
        from skimage.metrics import structural_similarity as ssim
        ssim_score, diff = ssim(gray1, gray2, full=True)
        
        # Feature matching
        orb = cv2.ORB_create()
        kp1, des1 = orb.detectAndCompute(gray1, None)
        kp2, des2 = orb.detectAndCompute(gray2, None)
        
        if des1 is not None and des2 is not None:
            bf = cv2.BFMatcher(cv2.NORM_HAMMING, crossCheck=True)
            matches = bf.match(des1, des2)
            match_score = len(matches) / max(len(kp1), len(kp2))
        else:
            match_score = 0
        
        return {

    def compare_objects(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:

    def compare_text_content(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:

    def compare_semantic(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray) -> Dict:

    def classify_changes(self, img1: np.ndarray, img2: np.ndarray,

    def detect_anomaly(self, comparison_results: Dict) -> Dict:

        return {'is_anomaly': False, 'anomaly_score': 0.0}

        features = []

    def heuristic_classification(self, differences: List) -> Dict:
        """Heuristic classification of changes."""
        if not differences:

    def generate_recommendations(self, results: Dict) -> List[str]:

content.title: Understanding Self-Healing Test Automation
content.explanation: Self-healing test automation refers to the ability of test scripts to automatically adapt to changes in the application under test, particularly changes to the user interface. Traditional test automation suffers from brittle locators that break when developers change HTML structure, CSS classes, or element IDs. Self-healing automation uses artificial intelligence to create resilient locators, detect when elements change, and automatically find alternative ways to interact with the application. This approach significantly reduces test maintenance overhead and improves test stability in dynamic development environments.

steps.title: Define Multiple Identification Strategies
steps.description: Create comprehensive element identification using multiple attributes
steps.details: Instead of relying on a single locator (like ID or XPath), capture multiple identification attributes for each element: ID, CSS class, XPath, text content, relative position, visual characteristics, and semantic context. Store these attributes in a structured format that allows fallback strategies when primary locators fail.

steps.title: Implement Dynamic Element Rediscovery
steps.description: Build algorithms to find elements when original locators fail
steps.details: When a locator fails, implement search algorithms that try alternative attributes. Use semantic similarity to find elements with similar text or functionality. Employ visual recognition to find elements that look similar. Leverage DOM structure analysis to find elements in similar positions relative to stable anchor elements.

steps.title: Create Learning and Adaptation Mechanisms
steps.description: Enable the system to learn from successful recoveries
steps.details: Track which locator strategies work best for different types of elements and pages. Use machine learning to predict which attributes are most stable for specific UI patterns. Automatically update locator strategies based on historical success rates. Implement confidence scoring for different identification methods.

steps.title: Integrate Computer Vision for Visual Recognition
steps.description: Add visual element recognition as a fallback strategy
steps.details: Capture visual signatures of important elements during test creation. Use template matching and feature detection algorithms to find elements visually. Implement OCR to read text from screenshots when DOM-based text extraction fails. Combine visual recognition with semantic understanding for robust element identification.

steps.title: Build Context-Aware Recovery Strategies
steps.description: Implement intelligent recovery based on page context
steps.details: Analyze the page structure and flow to understand what elements should be present. Use business logic and user journey understanding to predict expected elements. Implement recovery strategies tailored to specific failure patterns (login failures, navigation issues, form submission problems).

Increased test stability with fewer false positives from UI changes
Faster test execution through intelligent retry and recovery mechanisms
Better ROI on automation investment through reduced manual intervention
Improved developer productivity with fewer broken tests to fix
Enhanced test coverage through ability to handle dynamic content
Scalable test suites that can grow without proportional maintenance increase
